### Problem: same tree {#sec-tr-p2-same}

::: {.p-statement}
Two binary trees are the same when they have the same shape and equal values in corresponding nodes.

Constraints: each tree has at most $100$ nodes, values in $[-10^4, 10^4]$.

Source: [LC 100 · Same Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/same-tree/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
A difference is either a value or a missing node, and it sits at some pair of positions. Check that pair, then trust the same check on the two left children and on the two right children. Both empty is a match, not a failure.
:::

::: {#fig-tr-same}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):

    left = V.Node("1", [V.Node("2"), V.Node("3")], color="green")
    right = V.Node("1", [V.Node("2", color="red")], color="green")
    V.tree(ax, p, left, x=0.0, dx=1.15, dy=1.3, size=10)
    V.tree(ax, p, right, x=5.2, dx=1.15, dy=1.3, size=10)
    V.text(ax, p, 1.15, 1.2, "[1, 2, 3]", color="muted", size=9)
    V.text(ax, p, 5.2, 1.2, "[1, 2]", color="muted", size=9)

V.show(draw)
```

The same values where both trees have a node, and a missing child on the right. The pair $(3, \text{null})$ is the first failure. Both empty would be a match.

:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Recursion.** The template above. Return as soon as a pair disagrees.
2. **Level order.** Walk both trees with a queue of pairs. A null must be paired with a null. This is the same comparison with an explicit queue, which matters when the trees can be deep even if these constraints are not.

**Invariant.** If `same(p, q)` is true, every corresponding pair in the two subtrees has been compared.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
One call per pair of positions. Both null returns true before any value is read.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('same', 'rec')
    assert str(final) == 'False'
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def same_tree(p, q):
    if p is None or q is None:
        return p is q
    return p.val == q.val and same_tree(p.left, q.left) and same_tree(p.right, q.right)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool isSameTree(TreeNode* p, TreeNode* q) {
    if (!p || !q) return p == q;
    return p->val == q->val && isSameTree(p->left, q->left) && isSameTree(p->right, q->right);
}
```

:::

#### Level order

::: {.form-next}
The same three checks, pulled out of the call stack. Enqueue a pair only after both nodes exist.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('same', 'bfs')
    assert str(final) == 'False'
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def same_tree_bfs(p, q):
    qy = deque([(p, q)])
    while qy:
        a, b = qy.popleft()
        if a is None or b is None:
            if a is not b:
                return False
            continue
        if a.val != b.val:
            return False
        qy.append((a.left, b.left))
        qy.append((a.right, b.right))
    return True


a = from_level([1, 2, 3])
b = from_level([1, 2, 3])
c = from_level([1, 2, None])
assert same_tree(a, b) and same_tree_bfs(a, b)
assert not same_tree(a, c) and not same_tree_bfs(a, c)
assert same_tree(None, None) and not same_tree(Node(1), None)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool isSameTreeBfs(TreeNode* p, TreeNode* q) {
    queue<pair<TreeNode*, TreeNode*>> qu;
    qu.push({p, q});
    while (!qu.empty()) {
        auto [a, b] = qu.front();
        qu.pop();
        if (!a || !b) {
            if (a != b) return false;
            continue;
        }
        if (a->val != b->val) return false;
        qu.push({a->left, b->left});
        qu.push({a->right, b->right});
    }
    return true;
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
$O(n)$ time, where $n$ is the number of pairs examined. A mismatch at the root is $O(1)$. Stack or queue space is $O(h)$ or $O(\text{width})$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Two empty trees are the same. One empty tree and a single node are not.
- `[1,2]` and `[1,null,2]` have the same values in a different place. The null on the left of the second tree fails the pair.
- Equal values in a different shape are not the same tree. The structural test is the null check, not the value check.
- `[1,2,1]` and `[1,1,2]` have the same shape and different values.
- A preorder that writes `#` for every empty child separates `[1,2]` (`1,2,#,#,#`) from `[1,null,2]` (`1,#,2,#,#`). Values alone are `1, 2` for both.
- Both child pairs have to match. Accepting the tree when either pair matches reports equal trees that differ on one side.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Read a value only after both nodes exist. One empty side is already the answer, and it is false.
- Equal inorder sequences accept `[2, 1]` and `[1, null, 2]`. Both read `1 2`, and the trees differ. A traversal needs the missing children written down.
- `or` where the template has `and` accepts a tree that matches on only one side.
:::

**Variants.** A symmetric tree is this walk with the pairs crossed: [LC 101 · Symmetric Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/symmetric-tree/){difficulty="Easy"}. Starting the same walk at every node asks whether one tree is a subtree of the other: [LC 572 · Subtree of Another Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/subtree-of-another-tree/){difficulty="Easy"}. Flip equivalence tries the straight pairing and the crossed one: [LC 951 · Flip Equivalent Binary Trees](https://leetcode.com/problems/flip-equivalent-binary-trees/){difficulty="Medium"}. Exchanging the children, which builds the mirror, is @sec-tr-p2-invert.
